doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Joining Red Norvo and learning to arrange
summary: Meeting Norvo's band in Cleveland, joining, and being given the chance to write after Eddie Sauter.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: “What do you want to play?” And I said, “Confessing.” I played a chorus of “Confessing,” and he said all right, but you can’t — I was playing cornet — he said, “You can’t play on this you’ve got to get a trumpet. We drove clear back to Buffalo to a music store and got me a trumpet. Went back to Pittsburgh and I joined that band and that’s how, through that band, when we were working in Cleveland, Red Norvo’s band came. Mr. and Mrs. Swing came in to work the theater. And living at the Allerton Hotel in Cleveland, I used to hang out in the lobby with the guys from Red’s band, I loved that band. Dick’s band was good. So I had the opportunity to join Red so that was a change in my life too. Because that guy, I mean the learning process, I learned more music from that band. He gave me the opportunity to write. I didn’t write. I knew the scales and chords and progressions maybe but he would pay, minimally, I underline, but he’d pay me something to write arrangements for the band. And the arranger pre Rusty Dedrick, was Eddie Sauter. Eddie had left the band, he had played third trumpet with the band and wrote. He was one of my great idols you know.
So you had something to shoot for too, to follow him as an arranger.
Was there a certain process of writing something and hearing it—
That’s it. That’s exactly it, yes. That’s where Red afforded me that opportunity — to be able to try something, hear it played, and then make some adjustments and so forth. That was priceless.
You can’t have a better opportunity than that.

No. And as a teacher, we talk occasionally on the phone, you know he’s not well, he’s had a stroke and he’s incapacitated and he lives in California, but I said you know, “You were my teacher.” He doesn’t — you know. I just, I love him.
